args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api was deployed at v2.3.1 in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.

Action taken: Rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0, the most recent release with healthy status in production (v2.3.0 seq 1 healthy; v2.3.1 seq 3 unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and also unhealthy). The first rollback attempt halted with an orchestrator error after rolling out only us-east, leaving a mixed state (us-east v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still v2.3.1). A retry completed successfully and all three regions now report v2.3.0.

Current state: service healthy across all production regions, error rate 0.2% (down from 18%).

Follow-up needed: root-cause analysis of the v2.3.1 regression and why the initial rollback halted mid-rollout in us-west/eu-west. Do not redeploy v2.3.1 without approval.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did land (INC-0001) — the timeout was on the response, not the write. No duplicate created.

## Summary

**Done:**
1. **Diagnosed** — checkout-api was at v2.3.1 in all three production regions, unhealthy, 18% error rate. Release history showed v2.3.0 as the most recent production-healthy version (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy, so it was correctly excluded).
2. **Rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions** — the first attempt partially failed (`Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error`), leaving a mixed state with us-west and eu-west still on the bad v2.3.1. I verified state, retried, and all three regions now report v2.3.0.
3. **Verified recovery** — service healthy, error rate 0.2% (down from 18%).
4. **Opened INC-0001** — SEV2 for checkout-api, documenting the regression, the rollback, the partial-failure-and-retry, and follow-ups.

**On policy:** No approval was needed — I rolled back to v2.3.0, a version with confirmed healthy production history. I did not deploy any version that has never been healthy in production.

**Worth flagging for follow-up:** the orchestrator error that halted the first rollback mid-rollout is itself a reliability concern — a rollback that silently stops after one region leaves traffic split across a bad and good version, which is a worse failure mode than a clean failed rollback. That's captured in the incident summary for the on-call engineer.
